answers.question: What do you sell and to whom, and how many accounts?
answers.answer: B2B scheduling software for clinics, about 900 paying accounts at $79 a month per account.

answers.question: What is churn now and where does it sit?
answers.answer: 6.5% monthly overall (Stripe dashboard). I believe most of it is in months one to three.

answers.question: What data and tools can your AI reach?
answers.answer: Mixpanel usage and Intercom support through MCP read access; Stripe read-only. There is no cancellation survey.

answers.question: What is the goal and by when?
answers.answer: Overall monthly churn under 4% within two quarters.

answers.question: What may we change?
answers.answer: Onboarding, emails and in-app messages. Not pricing this year.

answers.question: Where should data live, and who decides?
answers.answer: In our Postgres analytics schema. I decide with the head of product.

answers.question: What is still unknown?
answers.answer: Whether clinics churn because of a missing integration.

research.approach: Practitioners start by fixing the definition of churn and counting it by sign-up cohort, so early churn is separated from later churn and from failed payments. They then find the product action that separates accounts that stay from those that leave, and read support conversations and cancellation reasons to learn why. Only then do they change onboarding, emails and in-app prompts, one at a time, and judge each against a comparison group of new accounts, because retention differences between cohorts alone are correlation.

sources.title: A primer on retention analytics for product leaders (Mixpanel)
sources.note: Define retention by meaningful product use, compare cohorts split by behaviour, and set aside churn that is not a problem.

sources.title: Churn rate benchmarks (Recurly)
sources.note: Splits voluntary from involuntary churn for B2B SaaS and points voluntary churn at onboarding and early product use; failed payments get their own fixes.

steps.name: Fix the churn definition and reconcile it with billing
steps.why: A blended 6.5% hides who leaves and when. Count by sign-up cohort and tenure, split choosing to leave from failed payments, and set aside leavers who got what they came for.

steps.name: Bring billing, usage and support data together by account
steps.why: Cohort and reason analysis need one row per account joining Stripe, Mixpanel and Intercom.

steps.name: Chart retention by sign-up cohort and find the activation action
steps.why: Show when accounts leave, then split by early product actions to find which one separates stayers from leavers.

steps.name: Learn why accounts leave from support conversations and cancellation reasons
steps.why: Usage shows what happened, not why. Support themes by tenure, including mentions of integrations, test the owner's open question; with no survey, a short cancel-reason prompt starts to fill the gap.

steps.name: Change first-use onboarding, emails and in-app messages as tests
steps.why: Fix the biggest gap before first value, one change at a time, with a comparison group so the effect can be read.

steps.name: Read results by cohort against the comparison group
steps.why: Churn falls only after accounts pass their early months, so activation and month-by-month retention of new cohorts are read first and overall churn last.

pitfalls.text: Treating a gap between retained and churned cohorts as proof the milestone causes retention; without a comparison group it is only correlation.
Mixing failed-payment churn with accounts that chose to leave, so onboarding gets blamed for a billing problem.
Spending effort on renewal-time saves and discounts while poor early engagement, the biggest driver of voluntary churn, goes unfixed.
Counting churn as lost accounts divided by all accounts, so new cohorts' early losses are diluted by older, stable accounts.

Share of accounts present in Stripe, Mixpanel and Intercom is reported, with unmatched accounts listed

stages.name: Check the 6.5% and the months one to three belief

Rebuilt churn is compared with the 6.5% reported; any gap is explained

stages.name: Find when accounts leave and what separates stayers
stages.goal: Chart retention by sign-up cohort, then compare early product actions of accounts that stayed with those that left to find a candidate activation action.

No card changes pricing

hypotheses.statement: Most churn sits in months one to three after sign-up.
hypotheses.test: Churn by tenure band for each sign-up cohort, rebuilt from account dates.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Months one to three account for the majority of cancels relative to their share of accounts.
hypotheses.refute_if: Churn is spread evenly across tenure, or sits mostly in later months.

hypotheses.statement: Accounts that do not reach a first-value action in their first weeks are the ones that leave.
hypotheses.test: Compare early actions of retained and churned accounts in Mixpanel; look for an action that separates them.
hypotheses.confirm_if: One early action separates stayers from leavers with enough accounts behind it.
hypotheses.refute_if: No early action separates the groups.

hypotheses.statement: Clinics leave because a needed integration is missing.
hypotheses.test: Count Intercom conversations that ask about or mention integrations before cancellation.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Integration requests appear in a clear share of cancelled accounts' conversations and less in retained ones.
hypotheses.refute_if: Integration mentions are rare or equally common among retained accounts.

hypotheses.statement: A meaningful part of early churn is failed payments, not a choice to leave.
hypotheses.test: Split cancels by chosen versus failed payment in Stripe.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Failed-payment cancels are a notable share of early churn.
hypotheses.refute_if: Nearly all early cancels are chosen.

hypotheses.statement: New accounts stall on setup questions that stay unresolved.
hypotheses.test: Support conversation volume, themes and resolution in the first 30 days for cancelled versus retained accounts.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Cancelled accounts show more unresolved setup conversations early.
hypotheses.refute_if: Early support patterns look the same for both groups.

hypotheses.statement: Some leavers are a poor fit for the product, so onboarding will not keep them.
hypotheses.test: Compare leavers and stayers on account attributes available in Stripe and Mixpanel, such as number of users and plan.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A recognisable account profile accounts for much of the early churn.
hypotheses.refute_if: Leavers look like stayers on every attribute we hold.

measurement.window: Read activation and month-one to month-three retention for each new sign-up cohort for at least 90 days after its change; read overall churn monthly against the same churn definition.
measurement.min_volume: Enough new accounts per comparison group to read, set in the test plan from the account counts; with about 900 accounts, expect small groups and wide uncertainty.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop a change early only if cancellations or support load rise clearly in the exposed group compared with the comparison group.
